comparison.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a gripper opening stop; PR-793 fits a rubber stopper at least 12 mm onto a glass tube while safely supporting the tube.
comparison.physical_skill: Both use two hands against reaction, but the candidate controls two concentric threaded elements with separate tools to prevent locknut-induced setpoint rotation; PR-793 grips fragile glass close to the work while pushing and twisting an interference-fit stopper.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires angular accuracy, seated retained nuts, tool withdrawal, three repeatable cycles, and low drift; PR-793 requires insertion depth and release, with zero for unsupported working or glass damage.
comparison.reason: Safe support during interference insertion does not subsume preservation of a calibrated threaded setting against its own locking torque and subsequent functional cycling; all versions expose the relevant safety and depth criteria.
